title: NAD+ decline and systemic metabolic rejuvenation
bottleneck: NAD+ levels fall with age across tissues, impairing sirtuins, DNA repair, and mitochondrial function, partly because the NAD+ consumer CD38 rises with age. Precursors like NMN and NR raise NAD+ in blood, but whether this translates to functional rejuvenation in human tissues is unproven, and the 2020s saw major NMN trials with underwhelming results.
why_it_blocks: NAD+ was the flagship metabolic-aging target with massive commercial hype; if precursors cannot show hard functional outcomes, it discredits the broader metabolic-rejuvenation thesis and the supplement-heavy funding model around it.
current_state: NMN/NR are widely sold as supplements while human trials test metabolic and muscle endpoints. CD38 inhibitors, which block NAD+ consumption rather than boosting supply, are the emerging pharmaceutical direction. Human trials of NMN raised blood NAD+ without consistent functional gains, shifting the field toward combination strategies and tissue-specific delivery rather than precursor monotherapy.
